reviewNotes: Handoff (SBAR), order tiers, and intervention mappings are proposed — not in the original case.
source: Instructor case: The Busy Med-Surg Shift — Patient 3
hpi: Harold was admitted three days ago with fever, productive cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe pneumonia. He has responded well to antibiotic therapy and is now feeling much better. He is eating and drinking adequately and has been ambulating in the hallway with minimal assistance. He lives at home with his wife, who is available to help him after discharge.

handoff.situation: 71M, hospital day 3 for RLL community-acquired pneumonia, improving.
handoff.background: HTN, T2DM, HLD. NKDA. Full code. Lives with wife.
handoff.assessment: Afebrile, SpO2 95% RA, pain 0/10. Mildly diminished RLL, occasional productive cough. Ambulating with minimal assist, eating well.
handoff.recommendation: Possible discharge today if criteria met. Needs med rec and discharge teaching.

baseline: Lung sounds mildly diminished in right lower lobe
Occasional productive cough with improving sputum
Ambulates independently or with minimal assistance

findings: States he is ready to go home and asks when he can leave
Unsure how long he needs to take his antibiotics
Unsure whether to keep using incentive spirometer at home

orders.text: Continue prescribed oral antibiotic until course completed
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Encourage coughing, deep breathing, and incentive spirometry
Discharge home today if clinically stable and discharge criteria are met
Follow up with primary care provider in 1 week
Notify provider for worsening respiratory symptoms, fever, or oxygen desaturation

payload.message: Harold told me he's ready to go home and asked when he can leave. He's not sure how long to take his antibiotics or if he should keep using his incentive spirometer at home.

shouldRecognize: Discharge planning can be delegated in appropriate portions, but the RN remains accountable for nursing assessment, discharge teaching, and evaluation of understanding.
Teach-back should be used to evaluate patient understanding.
Ensure the patient meets discharge criteria and that orders are complete.
Coordinate transportation, follow-up appointments, and prescriptions.
